a novel homozygous mutation (p.L673P) in AK7 causes MMAF and male infertility, but no PCD features; this mutation leads to a loss of the AK7 protein only in sperm flagella, and not in cilia of respiratory cells, suggesting a tissue-specific function of the protein in the two organelles.

we identified a homozygous missens mutation in AK7 gene in two siblings presenting asthenozoosperemia and MMAF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel genes causing male infertility and the characterization of their function in sperm flagella.
the identification of novel genetic causes of asthenozoöspemia and PCD, and it contributes to the understanding of the genetic and molecular bases of male infertility.
the identification of the first AK7 mutation in humans, and it provides new information on the function of this protein in the testis and in the sperm flagella.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AK7 mutation causes a sperm flagellum phenotype but not cilia phenotype.

AK7 is required for the assembly and function of sperm flagella but is dispensable in respiratory cilia, and that the AK7 mutation described here is the first human mutation in AK7 to be associated with asthenoteratozoospermia.
AK7 is not a ciliopathy gene, but rather an asthenozoospermiagenic gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the homozygous missence mutation L673P leads to primary male infertilit and multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella.
AK7 is required to maintain the structure and function of the sperm flagella, and that its mutation causes asthenozoosperemia and MMAF.
AK7, a protein that has a role in energy production and is shared by both ciliated and motile cilia, is essential in sperm flagella, but not in respiratory motile cilia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the same protein may have a specific function in different cellular compartments, and that mutations of this protein might lead to a spectrum of diseases, depending on which cellular compartment is mainly affected.
mutations in genes encoding proteins shared by both sperm flagella and respiratory cilia may lead to different phenotypes, in line with their different modes of assembly and function.
mutations in genes encoding proteins with preferential testis expression can cause asthenozoos spermia due to MMAFs without any PCD features.
